verdicts.text: New module code_open.py (stdlib only: os, io, json, re, tempfile). open_kind(path) -> {kind: 'lab'|'notebook'|'editor'|'text', reason, lines, marker, kernel}: .ipynb → 'lab'; .py/.R (case-insensitive) → count lines by streaming (stop counting at 121 — never read a huge file whole) and scan the first 5 non-blank lines for `# %%` (anywhere in the file counts as a cell marker, scanned up to the 121-line cap) or a `# notebook` marker; short (≤ 120 lines) OR marked → 'notebook', else 'editor'; kernel 'python3' for .py, 'ir' for .R; any other extension → 'text' (callers fall through to today's behaviour). Missing/unreadable file → {kind:'text', reason:'unreadable'} — never raises.
verdicts.need: John 2026-09-07: notebooks must come up when Python/R code is called 'at least if the code is descriptive/shorter'; 'longer bits of code can have a GUI that runs in a window ... like VS Code'
verdicts.rc2: Remove it and no surface can decide notebook-vs-editor-vs-lab; the user's short/long distinction — the core of the quote — is unimplementable for John. The ≤120 threshold is a tunable operationalization, not new scope.
verdicts.trigger: John ratifies that a long `# %%` or `# notebook` file opens as a notebook rather than the editor; that record then passes RC-1.
verdicts.needed_because: The classifier is the direct mechanism of the user's own short-code/long-code distinction; streaming line-count and never-raises keep it total over hostile inputs, matching the on-record honest-state convention.

verdicts.text: to_notebook(src_path, kernel, marker_split=False) -> {ok, ipynb_path, created: bool, reason}: sibling `<stem>.ipynb` in the same directory; if it ALREADY EXISTS return it with created=False and do not touch a byte (convert-once + never clobber a hand-edited notebook — the second call is byte-identical, asserted by hashing before/after in the test); otherwise write nbformat 4 / nbformat_minor 5 JSON: metadata.kernelspec {name:'python3'|'ir', display_name:'Python 3'|'R', language:'python'|'R'}, metadata.language_info {name}, cells = one code cell {cell_type:'code', id:<uuid4 hex[:8]>, metadata:{}, source:[lines with trailing \n except last], outputs:[], execution_count:null}; written via tempfile in the same dir + os.replace under paths.WRITE_LOCK. Hand-written writer — nbformat is NOT a dependency (distro.py import scan stays green).
verdicts.need: John 2026-09-07 (short code opens as a notebook — a .py has no notebook form without a converter) + CLAUDE.md stdlib-only rule (predates: distro.py import scan) forcing the hand-written writer
verdicts.rc2: Remove it and a short .py cannot open in JupyterLab at all — criterion of the user quote fails for John. Convert-once/never-clobber protects the user's hand-edited notebooks per the on-record copy-never-destroy convention (grass copy, Option A keep-docs).
verdicts.needed_because: No converter, no notebook for .py/.R; nbformat-as-dependency would break the on-record distro import-scan enforcement, so the hand-written writer is forced, not chosen.

verdicts.text: Judge decision carried as a flag, not a fork: marker_split=True splits on `# %%` lines into one code cell per block (a leading `# %% [markdown]` block becomes a markdown cell); recommendation to the Judge = split-on-marker when markers exist, one-cell when unmarked; default in the route is whatever the Judge locks — both paths share the writer and both are tested.

verdicts.text: New module live_links.py (stdlib: socket, subprocess, urllib.parse, json, time): allowed_hosts() -> frozenset lowercased = {'localhost','127.0.0.1', socket.gethostname().lower()} ∪ names from ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES (comma-separated override, e.g. `gwl-server,gwl-server.tailXXXX.ts.net`) ∪ (best-effort, 2 s timeout, cached 10 min, through an ANCHOR_TAILSCALE_CMD seam defaulting to `tailscale status --self --json`) the Self.HostName and Self.DNSName (trailing dot stripped). is_live_url(text) -> url|None: first http(s):// token in the cell; urllib.parse.urlsplit; scheme ∈ {http,https}; hostname (post-userinfo parsing, so `http://localhost@evil.example/` resolves to evil.example) must EQUAL an allowed host exactly (so `localhost.evil.com` and `evil.example` stay text); any port, any path; else None.

verdicts.text: Public API: start_lab(folder, project_id, health_timeout=20) -> {ok, lab_id, url, port, pid} | {ok:false, reason}; probe_lab(record, timeout=1.5) -> bool = GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/status with header `Authorization: token <token>` answers 200 (a live pid whose server hangs or answers 403 under a dead token counts as NOT ok — premortem 1); ensure_lab(folder, project_id) -> record: one live probing lab per project — if the registry has a running record that probes ok, return it; if it has a record whose pid is alive but the probe fails after 2 tries, tree-kill it (job_runner._tree_kill) and start fresh; serialized per project under a module lock so two clicks in the same second never start two labs; stop_lab(lab_id) tree-kills + status stopped; list_labs(project_id) reconciles dead pids → dead; reap_orphans() at boot RE-ADOPTS a record whose pid is alive AND probes ok (status stays running, the port and token are reused) and marks the rest dead — the plan does not assume a lab survives an NSSM restart either way.
verdicts.need: John 2026-09-07 'come up every time' — which forces start, a truthful liveness probe, idempotent ensure, and restart-of-dead; preview_server's list/stop/reap discipline on file
verdicts.rc2: Remove ensure/probe and a hung or token-dead lab yields the exact dead-click the journal-0110 workaround era produced; remove the per-project lock and two clicks mint two labs. 'Every time' is unimplementable without exactly this lifecycle. Re-adopt-on-boot vs restart is decided honestly (probe decides), not assumed.
verdicts.trigger: Same one-line as P2.1. If (B) is chosen, re-score ensure+probe against 'never a blank page'; the lock still needs a named double-spawn hazard or it stays cut.
verdicts.needed_because: This is the minimum lifecycle that makes the user's 'every time' true against the three observed-class failure modes (dead pid, hung server, stale token).
